problem_meta.instruction: Inspect the protein with the subsequent sequence and offer a concise description of its properties:
problem_meta.ground_truth: A brief overview of the protein with the provided amino acid sequence is as follows: Located at the top of the head of the 30S subunit, it contacts several helices of the 16S rRNA. In the 70S ribosome it contacts the 23S rRNA (bridge B1a) and protein L5 of the 50S subunit (bridge B1b), connecting the 2 subunits; these bridges are implicated in subunit movement. Contacts the tRNAs in the A and P-sites.
problem_meta.agent_answer:
1. [✓] Analyzed sequence properties and searched annotated homologs/functions.  
2. [✓] Recorded the finding in the evidence graph.  
3. [✓] Reviewed the stored evidence and summarized it.

**Functional summary:** This is bacterial ribosomal protein **uS13**, a component of the **30S small ribosomal subunit**. The 121-amino-acid sequence exactly matches reviewed UniProt protein **B1XSS4** (100% identity and coverage), and contains the **Ribosomal_S13** Pfam domain (PF00416; residues 3–108). uS13 binds 16S rRNA and contacts tRNAs in the A and P sites; in the assembled 70S ribosome, it also contributes to bridges linking the 30S and 50S subunits. Its annotated role is in ribosome structure and translation.

**Properties:** Estimated molecular mass **13.56 kDa**, theoretical pI **10.65**, and predicted charge at pH 7 of **+14.8**. These are sequence-derived estimates, not measurements.
